refs.description: Falsely and maliciously procuring another to be charged or arrested — the specific subdivision directly applicable to the 6/16/2023 setup and all prior false police report episodes. This is not a general theory; it is an enumerated criminal object.

Conspiracy to pervert or obstruct justice or the due administration of laws — reaches the coordinated court filing scheme, unsigned court documents, and jurisdictional manipulation across multiple tribunals.

Identity theft — conspiracy to commit § 530.5 carries elevated fine of up to $25,000 under § 182. The identity theft components of the scheme (stolen SSN, UA342 identity assumption) are objects of the conspiracy. Cross-reference pen_code_530_5_identity_theft.

Criminal threats — where threats were coordinated across multiple actors as part of the scheme, the threat-makers are co-conspirators and § 182(a)(1) conspiracy to commit § 422 applies. Cross-reference pen_code_422_criminal_threats.

Dissuading a witness — where multiple actors coordinated to prevent the steward from accessing legal remedies, reporting crimes, or testifying, the coordination is a § 182 conspiracy with § 136.1 dissuasion as one object.

False police report — where false reports were coordinated among multiple actors (e.g., reporting party + dispatcher + recipient of report), each participant is a conspirator under § 182(a)(1)/(a)(2). Cross-reference pen_code_148_5_false_police_report.

Federal conspiracy statute — where the scheme involved wire communications (phone calls, emails, texts) the federal conspiracy charge under § 371 may apply in parallel to the state § 182 charge. Federal venue may be more favorable.

Federal civil rights conspiracy — where the conspiracy involved state actors (law enforcement, CPS, court personnel), a § 1983 civil conspiracy claim is available in federal court alongside or instead of state § 182 charges. No criminal conviction required for the civil claim.
Jury instruction for conspiracy. Contains the dual intent requirement from People v. Beeman (1984). Defense and prosecution should review CALCRIM 415 for element structure.

Discovery — in any conspiracy prosecution, the identities, statements, and acts of all alleged co-conspirators are subject to § 1054.1 disclosure. Brady material includes all exculpatory evidence about any conspirator. Cross-reference pen_code_1054_1_discovery.
